extracted.intended_audience: general readers and fans seeking information about the Hot Ones show format, producers/researchers interested in the show's conventions
extracted.subtask_description: Documenting the rules, conventions, and recurring practices for producing/describing an episode of the Hot Ones YouTube talk show (number of wings, sauce progression, interview style, guest treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode core format — ten progressively hotter wings
rubrics_metrics.description: The format involves Evans and his celebrity guests eating ten chicken wings (or a vegetarian/vegan alternative), each prepared with a progressively hotter hot sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first sauce is relatively mild (example: sriracha ~2,200 Scoville units). After each wing Evans usually asks his guest an interview question. As the wings get hotter, guests typically begin to display the effects of eating spicier wings and the interview dynamic shifts. The standard show is Evans and one guest eating ten wings each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vegetarian/vegan alternative allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests may be given a vegetarian/vegan alternative based on the guest's preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show substitutes non-meat wings when requested so the progressive-heat format can be preserved for guests who do not eat chicken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final sauce placement and tradition — 'The Last Dab' as final sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: The final sauce is Hot Ones' own The Last Dab (with named variants across seasons) and occupies the final spot; guests are encouraged to put a minuscule extra amount of The Last Dab on the final wing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variants named on the page include The Last Dab Reduxx (starting season 6), The Last Dab XXX (starting Season 10), The Last Dab Apollo (starting season 13), and The Last Dab Xperience (starting in season 22). Guests are told adding the extra dab is not required, but most opt to do so even when already struggling. The Last Dab's Scoville rating is noted as 2,000,000+.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurring sauce-lineup conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each season features a different line-up of hot sauces, though certain sauces remain from year-to-year, including three self-produced sauces placed in particular spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: 'Hot Ones – The Classic' typically in spot 1; 'Hot Ones – Los Calientes' in either spot 4 or 5; 'Hot Ones – The Last Dab' as the final sauce. Since Season 2, 'Da' Bomb Beyond Insanity' has occupied spot 8. Guidance implies deliberate sequencing to shape difficulty and interview progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview question progression (softball → deeply researched)
rubrics_metrics.description: After each wing Evans usually asks his guest an interview question, starting with easy 'softball' questions and moving to more deeply researched and personal questions as the wings get hotter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes the questions often become more deeply researched and personal as the episode proceeds, and the guest's increasing reaction to spice affects the tone and content of the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest reaction-driven shift in interview focus
rubrics_metrics.description: If the guest struggles to finish the wings, the interview becomes less focused on the questions and more on the guest's reaction to the spice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a built-in dynamic of the format: as physical effects mount, conversational priorities shift from promotion/Q&A to genuine reaction and banter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of soothing condiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests are furnished with whatever soothing condiments they think will counteract the effect of the wings, including glasses of water and milk as well as ice cream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The show supplies common spice-relief items; these are part of the episode conventions and visible in episodes when guests need relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode composition exceptions — two guests and reduced-wing specials
rubrics_metrics.description: While the standard show is Evans and one guest eating ten wings each, some episodes have two guests and a few (mostly specials) present five wings instead of ten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page cites specific episodes with two guests (e.g., Keegan-Michael Key and Jordan Peele; Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman). Specials may alter the wing count to fit format variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest post-interview promotion practice
rubrics_metrics.description: To finish off, Evans encourages his guests to promote their upcoming projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conventional closing practice: after the gauntlet, guests usually get space to mention/promote current or upcoming work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-to-finish consequence — Hall of Shame / 'Wall-Most Made it'
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests who do not complete the gauntlet of hot sauces are placed in the 'Hall of Shame' or, beginning in Season 17, the 'Wall-Most Made it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recurring ranking/recognition convention used by the show to mark finishing status. It functions as a light competitive/archival element of the series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable quality criterion — deep-probing questions praised
rubrics_metrics.description: The show has been noted for its deep-probing questions, often digging up material from a celebrity's background not often discussed on other interview shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party commentary (e.g., Hollywood Insider) characterizes the interview style as 'the hottest celebrity interview right now' because of its probing questions — this functions as a qualitative standard for what makes the show notable or 'good' as an interview format.
